models.notes: Document-conversion specialist. Emits DocTags markup with a bounding box, page index, and structural role per element.
Generalist chat VLM. Prompted directly for an APR-shaped intermediate JSON (sections/fields/labels/types).

OCR/layout specialist. No genuine MLX build existed on the Hub (the only 'dots.ocr-4bit' upload found was bitsandbytes-quantized, incompatible with mlx-vlm) so this was converted in-house from dots-studio/dots.ocr via `mlx_vlm convert --quantize --q-bits 4`. Native output is a JSON list of {bbox, category, text} per detected element.

Pure grounding/detection specialist (task-token interface, no chat). Used with <OCR_WITH_REGION>; label/field pairing is done by a deterministic geometry heuristic in this harness, not by the model. NOTE: Florence-2-large-ft-4bit and -bf16 both hit a confirmed mlx-vlm compatibility bug (the model only ever emits the BOS token, verified empirically) as of mlx-vlm 0.7.0 in Sept 2026 -- base-ft is the variant that actually works, so it stands in for the whole Florence-2 family here. This is a real, reportable finding, not a benchmark design choice.

Smaller sibling of qwen3-vl-8b, same family/prompt/strategy. Added to answer the resource-load question directly: does the 8B's quality (and its very slow per-page time, often 100-200s+) actually require 8B, or does 4B get most of the way there in a fraction of the time.

Second generalist chat VLM family (92.7 DocVQA at 8B per its own paper), same intermediate-JSON prompt as Qwen3-VL, to check whether Qwen's results reflect the model or just the default assumption of 'Qwen is best'.

Substituted for Moondream2: vikhyatk/moondream2's own config.json declares model_type 'moondream1', which mlx-vlm's registry does not implement (only moondream2/moondream3) -- a confirmed, real incompatibility, not a workaround-able prompting issue. PaliGemma 2 fills the same 'detection/grounding specialist, second opinion vs. Florence-2' niche and has confirmed real mlx-community builds. Google's own training mixture includes OCR-with-localization producing {transcription, bbox} pairs. First run used greedy decoding (temperature=0, uniform across all 7 models for fairness) which sent this model into repetition loops on several forms (one page repeated "Corporation" until the token cap, producing 2005 spurious 'fields'); repetition_penalty=1.3 confirmed empirically to eliminate the loop without changing temperature.
